thesis.what_must_be_true: For the story to hold, AMAT must convert the record AI-driven order book into >25% y/y revenue growth through calendar 2026 while expanding GAAP operating margin toward 33% and normalizing the working-capital build that compressed FCF in Q2 — with FCF recovering in 2H26 and cash generation funding both the rising dividend and continued buybacks.

validated.preview_note: AMAT reports FQ3 (July-end) with the Street anchoring on management's $8.95B ±$500M revenue and $3.36 ±$0.20 non-GAAP EPS guide — a step-up from the record $7.91B quarter that broke out on AI-led logic/DRAM/HBM and advanced-packaging strength. Three factors decide the reaction. First, revenue conversion: the CEO's >30% calendar-2026 semi-equipment growth call requires the record backlog to ship; anything near the $9.3B high end signals sustained momentum, below $8.4B breaks the narrative. Second, margin resilience: gross margin held ~50% in Q2 despite the build; with DRAM/HBM mix strong but advanced-packaging and inventory-build costs rising, holding 49%+ while pushing operating margin toward 33% is the swing factor on EPS. Third, free cash flow: Q2 FCF collapsed to $210M on an inventory/logistics build that management flagged as deliberate supply-chain readiness. The market will pay up for the growth if FCF inflects back above ~$850M and Q4 guidance confirms another sequential step-up (>$9.3B). A print that delivers record revenue, steady margins and a FCF recovery would confirm the multi-year AI capex supercycle; a guide-down or margin miss would justify derating the capital-return story.
validated.reasoning: I anchored every historic figure to AMAT's as-filed record: FQ2 revenue $7,910M, gross profit $3,947M, operating income $2,523M, net income $2,806M, GAAP EPS $3.51, non-GAAP EPS $2.86, FCF $210M, cash+restricted $6,359M, retained earnings $59,274M, total equity $23,909M (accessions 0001628280-26-035071 and -037227), and FQ1 non-GAAP EPS $2.38. Guidance mid for FQ3 is $8,950M revenue and $3.36 non-GAAP EPS. I hold revenue at guidance mid (8,950), model a ~49.5% gross margin (cost 4,503 → gross 4,447), opex of 1,445 (R&D up modestly to 1,030 on EPIC investment), giving operating income of 3,002; with net interest/other income of 290 (including strategic-investment income) pretax is 3,292 and a ~11% effective tax yields net income 2,932, GAAP EPS $3.71 on 790M shares. The bridge lands non-GAAP net income at 2,654 (adjustments −278), i.e. non-GAAP EPS $3.36 = guidance mid. Cash flow: CFO 1,640 (net income + D&A 155 + SBC 190 less heavy working-capital other of −1,637), capex −750, FCF 890; CFI −1,000 (including investment purchases), CFF −1,310 (buybacks −900, dividends −420 at the raised $0.53, other +10), net change −670 to cash of 5,689. Balance sheet rolls: retained 60,886 (59,274+2,932−420−900), total assets 51,000 = cash 5,689 + other 45,311 = liabilities 21,500 + equity 29,500. Later quarters step revenue up ~5-8% q/q through FQ4'27 on the AI cycle, with FCF recovering as working capital normalizes. Horizons FY26-29 reflect high-teens growth decelerating to ~9% by FY29.
